source.title: Beyond BatchNorm: Towards a Unified Understanding of Normalization in Deep Learning
source.authors: E. Lubana; Robert P. Dick; Hidenori Tanaka

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The paper experimentally measures how normalization choices affect training curves and training stability on CIFAR-100, and analyzes initialization-time activation and gradient properties. This conceptually tests V6's normalization/training-speed claim with different measures and recipes.
record.gate_note: Own training curves, activation measurements, and gradient measurements bear on V6. Claims and results attributed to cited prior work are not rows. Figure 1 and Appendix Figures 11–14 report curves without tabulated terminal values; rows record only explicit textual outcomes where available. The paper does not test versions V1, V2, V3, V4, or V5.
record.test_reason: The study compares alternative normalization methods and explains their training behavior. It does not report training-speed or learning-rate comparisons between otherwise identical networks with and without normalization, or test Fixup. Initialization-time activation and gradient measurements do not establish the initialization, depth-degradation, or stability-threshold effects named in the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors extend initialization-time explanations of BatchNorm to alternative normalizers, identify architecture-dependent failures and a GroupNorm speed–stability trade-off, and argue that properties shared with alternatives leave BatchNorm's particular success requiring further explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies normalization layers and their effects on activation statistics, gradient norms, and CIFAR-100 training curves, rather than the original claim's comparison of BatchNorm training speed across specified datasets and architectures. It also changes residual-path architecture in one experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with normalization method, network architecture, batch size, initial learning rate, and residual-path design. The authors report increasing GroupNorm group size decreases gradient explosion while increasing activation similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: LayerNorm often converges slowly; Instance Normalization becomes unstable in deeper plain networks or with small batches; Weight Normalization fails in the tested ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training speed and stability depend on the normalization method, architecture, batch size, and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Moving the non-linearity onto the residual path enables parametric normalizers to match BatchNorm performance in several configurations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual-path design can determine whether parametric normalization trains successfully.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation similarity at initialization predicts mean training accuracy; smaller GroupNorm groups reduce similarity while increasing gradient amplification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GroupNorm group size trades informative representations against gradient stability.

record.problems: Most training outcomes are shown in plots rather than numerically reported in text. The paper reports averages over 3 seeds with standard deviation bars for training curves, but does not give tabulated terminal training accuracy. The experiments are limited to discriminative vision tasks, mainly CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were added for the many individual normalizer-by-batch-size-by-architecture curves in Figures 11–14 because exact per-curve measurements are figure-only and would require reconstructing values. The figure-level aggregate outcomes are represented in R1–R4 and the explicit textual summary in R5.

untested.parts: Attainment of zero or near-zero training classification error, including random-label conditions and model-size dependence; no readable terminal values establish this outcome.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the named alternative initialization recipes.
Comparative training speed and trainable depth under activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and orthogonal convolution kernels.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Speed and learning-rate tolerance from adding BatchNorm to otherwise identical networks without normalization, and normalization-free training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study reports its own optimization experiments, but their normalization-method contrasts do not directly test the versions supplied. No verdict follows merely from an alternative method failing or matching BatchNorm accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Training from random initialization to near-zero classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and extra student width.
Whether plain networks degrade with depth compared with residual shortcuts, and the specified alternative initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain network trainability.
Training behavior above the stability limit and sharpness dynamics.

The paper tests CIFAR-100 vision networks and reports faster/slower convergence or instability across normalization methods. It does not test sigmoid networks on MNIST, VGG on CIFAR-10, Inception on ImageNet, or Fixup residual networks.

rows.subject: 10-layer non-residual CNN
rows.operation_detail: Train/test curves for different normalizers at largest stable initial learning rate; 3 seeds.

conditions.value: multiple methods in Figure 1 and Appendix Figure 11

rows.uncertainty: 3 seeds; error bars ± standard deviation in Appendix Figure 11
rows.note: The text reports LayerNorm often converges slowly and Instance Normalization can be unstable with depth or small batches; the figure's per-method values are not stated in prose.
rows.check: Aggregates multiple normalizers and batch sizes rather than recording individual comparisons. The supplied text does not preserve readable curves, and no training comparison with an unnormalized control is reported.

rows.subject: ResNet-56 (with SkipInit)
rows.operation_detail: Train/test curves for different normalizers at largest stable initial learning rate; 3 seeds.

conditions.value: multiple methods in Figure 1 and Appendix Figure 14

rows.uncertainty: 3 seeds; error bars ± standard deviation in Appendix Figure 14
rows.note: The text explicitly says Weight Normalization cannot be trained for ResNets with and without SkipInit; other per-method outcomes are presented graphically.
rows.check: Comparisons among normalizers with SkipInit do not test the specified Fixup recipe or isolate adding BatchNorm. Weight Normalization's failure should be recorded separately from the other methods.

rows.subject: normalization methods across evaluated configurations
rows.size_stated: hundreds of models evaluated; three architectures described
rows.operation_detail: Authors summarize observed training speed and instability across normalizers, architectures, batches, and learning rates.

conditions.value: different normalizer, network architecture, batch size, and learning rate

rows.baseline: BatchNorm and other normalizers compared across configurations
rows.value: LayerNorm often converges relatively slowly; Weight Normalization cannot be trained for ResNets with and without SkipInit; Instance Normalization is unstable in deeper non-residual networks, especially with small batches.
rows.note: Supports a normalization-related speed/stability effect while showing it depends on the normalization method and configuration.
rows.check: Combines distinct speed and instability outcomes across methods and architectures. Slow LayerNorm and unstable Instance or Weight Normalization do not qualify a claim specifically about BatchNorm versus its absence.

rows.subject: ResNet-56 with parametric normalizers
rows.operation_detail: Move the non-linearity to the residual path and compare training performance with BatchNorm.

conditions.value: Weight Normalization and Scaled Weight Standardization

rows.baseline: BatchNorm performance; exact values not stated
rows.value: These models are able to match BatchNorm in performance for several training configurations.
rows.uncertainty: over 3 seeds; exact error bars not stated in the text
rows.note: A normalization-free residual recipe is not tested; this is a changed residual architecture with parametric normalization.
rows.check: Matching BatchNorm performance after changing residual-path architecture and using parametric normalization does not establish equal training speed, learning-rate tolerance, or the Fixup result. The recorded observed state is therefore unjustified against V6.
